samples.summary: Design doc names a helper that does not exist and mis-scopes it. `docs-tables.md` (and the lessons doc) describe `removeCellNodeStyle` in `yorkie-doc-store.ts`, but the implemented helper is `removeNodeStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:273) and it is not cell-specific — it is also the removal path for block-type attributes (`setBlockType`, line 1459). Nested design docs are not link/path-checked by CI, so nothing else will catch the drift; the canonical description of a shared helper should name it correctly and say it covers block nodes too.

Scope well beyond the originating issue. #728 (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md) has a single acceptance criterion — resetting the text color paints default ink, not the selection color — and non-goals limited to picker UI and migrations. This change additionally lands: a full slides-arm PUT validation walker (layout placeholders/staticElements, slide notes, group children, table-cell bodies), a shared Yorkie attribute codec extraction, node-scoped Yorkie attribute removal, a PPTX preset-geometry allowlist, `lvl` clamping and `ST_Percentage` coercion. Each is defensible hardening, but none is required by the acceptance criterion, and bundling them makes the change hard to review/revert as one unit. (The lessons doc suggests prior review rounds asked for some of it, hence medium confidence.)
samples.evidence: assertValidHeaderFooter / assertValidLayout / assertValidSlideBlocks added alongside the #728 color fix; PRST_BY_KIND added in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts

samples.summary: `PRST_BY_KIND` hand-duplicates the `ShapeKind` union (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:54-125) as a runtime list. `as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>[]` only checks that listed members are valid — it does not check exhaustiveness — so a shape kind added to the union later compiles fine and silently exports as `rect`, corrupting geometry in every generated .pptx with no test or type error. If a runtime allowlist is wanted, derive it from a single source (e.g. a `Record<Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>, string>` literal, which does force exhaustiveness) rather than a parallel array.
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts: `] as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind, 'freeform'>[]` and `return PRST_BY_KIND.get(kind) ?? 'rect';`

samples.summary: The PPTX export design doc still states `kind`→`prstGeom prst` as the plain inverse of the importer's map and does not record the new behaviours this change introduces at that sink: an unknown/untrusted `kind` now degrades to `rect`, and `<a:pPr lvl>` is now truncated/clamped to [0,8] with out-of-range values dropping the attribute. The colour section was updated but these two behaviour changes were not, leaving the canonical subsystem doc stale for exported geometry and list levels.

Alias-only indirection: `toDocxHexColor` is a one-line re-export of `toRgbHexColor` with no added behaviour, and both Yorkie stores introduce `const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs` / `parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs` (plus `serializeMarginFromEdge`, `parseMarginFromEdge`) purely to preserve old local names. Importing the shared names directly would remove three layers of naming that readers must chase.
samples.evidence: `export function toDocxHexColor(color) { return toRgbHexColor(color); }`; docs-tree.ts `const serializeBlockStyle = serializeBlockStyleAttrs;`

finding.summary: Slides PUT block-style validation is advertised as covering "every text body" but skips `slide.notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements`, and `masters[]` — the same partial-coverage failure the task's own lessons doc calls out
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only checks `Array.isArray(s.notes)` and then walks `s.elements`; `assertValidSlidesBody` checks `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays and never descends into them. But `Slide.notes: Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and `Layout.placeholders: PlaceholderSpec[]` / `staticElements: Element[]` (presentation.ts:61-62) hold the same docs `Block`s reaching the same layout engine (see packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts). docs/design/rest-api.md (new text) states: "the same block-style value checks are applied to the docs `Block`s inside every text body — text elements, shape text, table cells and group children", and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:71-73 records the rule "a validator that walks only one of the writer's inputs is worse than none, because it reads as coverage." A `NaN` marginTop or unknown alignment can still be PUT through `slides[i].notes[0].style` or through a layout placeholder.

verdict.reason: The claimed coverage gaps do not exist in this tree. `assertValidSlide` walks `slide.notes` through `assertValidSlideBlocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:555-557), which applies `assertValidBlockStyle` with the numeric-finiteness and alignment checks (lines 692-703, 330-358) — so a NaN marginTop in `slides[i].notes[0].style` is rejected, contrary to the finding. `assertValidSlidesBody` does descend into layouts: lines 493-496 iterate `layouts` into `assertValidLayout`, which walks both `placeholders` and `staticElements` via `assertValidNestedElement` → `assertValidElementData` → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (lines 499-516, 595-642). `masters[]` needs no walk because `Master` is `{ id, themeId, background, placeholderStyles }` with `PlaceholderStyle = { fontRole, fontSize, colorRole, align, lineHeight }` (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:4-34) — it holds no Element and no docs Block, so there is no text body inside it. All three cited fields (presentation.ts:45, 61, 62) are covered or vacuous.
